Closes #

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (`fix`)
- [ ] New feature (`feat`)
- [ ] Refactoring with no behavior change (`refactor`)
- [ ] Performance (`perf`)
- [ ] Tests only (`test`)
- [ ] Documentation only (`docs`)
- [ ] Translations (`i18n`)
- [ ] Security hardening (`security`)
- [ ] CI, build or maintenance (`ci`, `build`, `chore`)

## Checklist

### Branch and title

- [ ] The base branch is `dev`.
- [ ] The title follows the Conventional Commit format `type(scope): subject`.

### Gates

Run from the repository root. All three must pass.

- [ ] `npm run lint --workspace=app`
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit --project app/tsconfig.json`
- [ ] `npm run test:coverage --workspace=app` (only the coverage run enforces the thresholds in `app/vitest.config.ts`)

### Area and CI-parity checks

Tick what you ran. For the others, write "not applicable: <area> not touched" or "not run, because ..." next to the item.

- [ ] `lobby/`: `npm run lobby:typecheck`
- [ ] `infra/recorder/` or `infra/recorder-controller/`: in that folder, `npm ci`, then `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && npm test`
- [ ] `infra/ai/worker/`: in that folder, `pip install -r requirements-test.txt`, then `python -m pytest -q`
- [ ] `infra/helm/`: `./scripts/validate-chart.sh`
- [ ] Live-room flows: the E2E smoke tests, `npx playwright test --project=chromium` from `app/` against the local stack
- [ ] Security Scan, on every change: `trivy fs --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --exit-code 1 .` from the repository root. It also looks for secrets in every file.
- [ ] Docker Build & Scan, on any change except documentation-only changes: `docker build -t pa-webinar:local .`, then `trivy image --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --exit-code 1 pa-webinar:local`
- [ ] License Compliance when a dependency changed, and Migration Integrity when `app/prisma/` changed, with the commands in the [CI-parity table](https://github.com/italia/pa-webinar/blob/dev/docs/development/methodology.md#ci-parity-before-every-push)

### Content rules

- [ ] New logic has tests.
- [ ] Every new interface string exists in all 24 catalogs in `app/src/i18n/messages/`, with real translations rather than the English copies that `scripts/sync-i18n.mjs` fills in. No text is hardcoded in components.
- [ ] Every new page is declared in the `pathnames` map in `app/src/i18n/routing.ts`.
- [ ] A change to `app/prisma/schema.prisma` comes with the migration SQL generated by `npm run db:migrate:dev --workspace=app`, in the same commit. The migration is additive, and no released migration is edited.
- [ ] A dependency change comes with `license-report.json` regenerated by `npm run license:report` and committed together with `package-lock.json`.
- [ ] A new model that holds participants' personal data is purged by the `/api/cron/cleanup` transaction and covered by its test, and it is classified in `app/src/lib/gdpr/cleanup-coverage.ts`. If the model points to a stored file, the cleanup deletes the file too. The guard test sees only tables with an `eventId` column, so check any other model by hand.

### Documentation, roadmap and changelog

- [ ] The page in `docs/` that owns the behavior describes it as it is after this change. The [documentation index](https://github.com/italia/pa-webinar/blob/dev/docs/README.md) lists the owner pages.
- [ ] If this delivers an item of the [roadmap](https://github.com/italia/pa-webinar/blob/dev/docs/ROADMAP.md), the description names it. The item leaves the roadmap with the release that ships it.
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` is not edited. It is generated from the release notes, which are written when a release is prepared.

### Public repository

- [ ] No personal data: no names, email addresses or IP addresses of real people in code, fixtures, logs, screenshots or this description.
- [ ] No secrets. The development placeholders in `docker-compose.yml` and `.env.example` are unchanged, and `.env.example` does not gain `ALLOW_INSECURE_PII_KEY`.
- [ ] No internal names (events, meetings, people, ticket codes) and no data from a real environment (hosts, IP addresses, cluster, namespace or secret names). Examples use placeholders such as `webinar.example.com`, `<namespace>` and RFC 1918 addresses.

### Shared contracts and defaults

- [ ] This changes a shared contract or a default: a response shape, a guard, an enum value, a token rule, an i18n key used elsewhere, or a default in `values.yaml`, `schema.prisma` or the site settings. The consumers you checked are listed under "How it was verified".

### Review

- [ ] I reviewed my own diff for regressions: callers of what I changed, paths through any guard I added or removed, readers of anything I renamed, and defaults that change under running installations.
- [ ] Reviewer (tick before merging): a non-trivial change (behavior, response contracts, guards, data model, interface logic or strings) has had its code review, and every confirmed finding is fixed or accepted explicitly in this pull request.
